subject: English
passage: In 1965 Nancy Hanks was chosen to head the newly established National Endowment for the Arts (NEA). This organization was part of the Great Society initiative, a program created by President Lyndon B. Johnson to expand cultural and educational opportunities across America. As the chairwoman of the NEA, Hanks distributed grants to over 8,000 artists, museums, and cultural organizations throughout the nation. She also prioritized funding for programs in underserved communities, which meant that many people could access professional arts programming for the first time.
prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.A: Grants provided by the NEA were intended mainly for artists, museums, and cultural organizations.
choices.B: As the chairwoman of the NEA, Hanks succeeded in distributing funding and expanding arts access to new communities.
choices.C: President Johnson created the Great Society initiative to expand cultural and educational opportunities.
choices.D: During the 1960s, many communities lacked access to professional arts programming.

explanation:
Choice B is the best answer because it most accurately states the main idea of the text. The text begins by stating that Hanks was chosen in 1965 to head the National Endowment for the Arts (NEA), which was part of a program created by President Lyndon B. Johnson. The text then explains that as the chairwoman of the NEA, Hanks distributed grants to more than 8,000 cultural recipients and prioritized funding for underserved communities so that many people could access professional arts programming for the first time. Thus, the main idea of the text is that as the NEA's chairwoman, Hanks succeeded in distributing funding and expanding arts access to new communities.

Why C is incorrect:

Choice C is incorrect. The text does state that President Johnson created the Great Society initiative to expand cultural and educational opportunities, but this is supporting information, not the text's main idea. The focus of the text is Nancy Hanks's work as the chairwoman of the NEA, which was part of the Great Society initiative, and the text's main point is that Hanks succeeded in distributing funding and expanding arts access to new communities.
